title: Christian Living - Episode 6: The Quiet Fruit of the Spirit

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Good evening, and welcome back to the SleepFit podcast series. <short pause> This is Christian Living, episode six: The Quiet Fruit of the Spirit. <chuckle> I'm David Lee. <short pause> And tonight is a special one... <short pause> because this is the final episode of our series. <chuckle> But don't worry... <short pause> this isn't goodbye forever. <short pause> I'm sure we'll meet again. <long pause>

It's been a quiet joy to spend these evenings with you. <short pause> So before we go, I'd like to ask one last question... <short pause> what does it look like, when God changes us from the inside? <long pause>

Paul gives us a picture in his letter to the Galatians. <short pause> He's writing to people who thought they had to earn God's favor by following rules perfectly. <short pause> They were wearing themselves out, trying to be good enough. <short pause> And Paul says... you're looking at this all wrong. <long pause>

He contrasts two ways of living. <short pause> One is driven by what he calls the flesh... our own striving, our appetites, our anxious effort to secure ourselves. <short pause> The other is led by the Spirit... God's presence, quietly at work in us. <short pause> And then he describes what grows, when the Spirit leads. <long pause>
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Notice he calls it fruit... not fruits. <short pause> It's not a checklist of nine separate virtues you try to manufacture. <short pause> It's one crop. One harvest. All the qualities flowing from the same root. <long pause>

And fruit doesn't grow by willpower. <short pause> An apple doesn't appear because the branch tries hard. <short pause> It appears because the branch is connected to the tree... and the life of the tree flows into it. <short pause> So love, joy, peace... these aren't things you produce by clenching your fists, and resolving to do better. <short pause> They grow... when you stay connected to Christ. <long pause>

Look at the first three. Love, joy, peace. <short pause> These are about how you relate to God, and receive from him. <short pause> The next three... longsuffering, gentleness, goodness. <short pause> These are about how you relate to other people. <short pause> And the last three... faith, meekness, temperance. <short pause> These are about the inward ordering of your own heart. <long pause>
And none of it is frantic. <short pause> None of it is about performing, or impressing, or meeting a quota. <short pause> It's quiet growth... slow, and real. <long pause>
Paul goes on. <long pause>
And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit. <long pause>

If his life is in us... then we walk in step with him. <short pause> That word, walk, is important. <short pause> Walking isn't dramatic. It's just one foot in front of the other... steady, and unhurried. <short pause> You don't walk by straining, or by mapping out every step a mile ahead. <short pause> You walk by paying attention to where you are... and moving with the rhythm that's already there. <long pause>
This is how the Christian life actually works. <short pause> Not by heroic effort... but by quiet attentiveness to the Spirit's presence. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> Now, if you're listening to this at the end of a long day, you might be thinking... I didn't see much fruit today. <short pause> I was impatient. I was anxious. I wasn't very gentle. <short pause> And that's okay. <long pause>

Fruit grows slowly. <short pause> You don't inspect an apple tree every evening, and worry that it's failing because the apples aren't ripe yet. <short pause> God isn't disappointed in you, because the fruit isn't finished. <short pause> He's the gardener... and he's patient. <long pause>

Your part isn't to manufacture the fruit. <short pause> Your part is just to stay connected. <short pause> To come back to him... to let him speak to you... to trust that his life is flowing into yours, even when you can't see it. <long pause>

Maybe today you noticed one small moment of patience, where there used to be none. <short pause> Maybe you felt a flicker of peace, in a situation that usually makes you anxious. <short pause> That's the fruit, beginning to show. <short pause> And it's not because you worked up the strength to be patient, or peaceful. <short pause> It's because the Spirit was at work in you... quiet, and steady. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So tonight, you don't have to resolve to be better tomorrow. <short pause> You don't have to make a list of virtues to practice. <short pause> You can simply rest in the truth that you are connected to Christ... and his life is in you. <short pause> The fruit will come in its time. <long pause>

Thank you for walking through this series with me. <short pause> Whenever you need a quiet place to land, you can come back to any of these evenings. <short pause> And wherever you go from here... may you stay close to him. <long pause>

Let's pray. <long pause> Father, thank you that you don't ask us to produce fruit by our own effort... but that you grow it in us by your Spirit. <short pause> Help us to stay connected to you... to walk in step with you... and to trust your quiet work in our hearts. <long pause>
Rest well tonight. <short pause> God is with you. <short pause> Goodnight.
